qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Infill locations across high-growth Sunbelt metros (Atlanta, Dallas, Charlotte, Tampa, Orlando, Nashville) offer local clustering scale, but low municipal entitlement and zoning barriers allow merchant builders to introduce massive competing multi-family supply waves during expansion cycles. Empirically, 5-year and 10-year median GAAP ROIC is ~5.0%–5.2%, far below the 12% threshold. One-year leases and negligible tenant switching costs leave MAA as a price-taker during supply delivery peaks.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 5.2% vs. 12% hurdle; price-taker in Sunbelt supply waves, REJECT). While rental housing serves a basic human need and MAA maintains an investment-grade balance sheet, residential real estate is inherently capital-intensive with unlevered returns structurally capped at 4%–6% cap rates. Short one-year tenant leases and persistent new multifamily supply across Sunbelt submarkets prevent sustained above-inflation pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year and 10-year median GAAP ROIC hovers around 5.0%–5.2% (FY24 ~5.9%, FY25 ~5.5%, FY26 ~5.1%), far below the 12% hurdle. Diluted FFO per share declined from $8.77 in FY24 to $8.32 in FY25, with FY26 guidance of $8.41–$8.65 reflecting persistent multi-family supply deliveries across core Sunbelt markets. Although leverage is prudent (~4.0x Net Debt/EBITDAre) and AFFO safely covers the dividend, returns on capital are structurally below the quality compounder threshold.
